summary.oneLiner: Cash-rich, founder-run conglomerate where Zambian thermal IPP (Maamba) drives consolidated profit and funds a multi-pronged diversification (300MW thermal expansion, 100MW solar, sugar, avocado, lithium/mineral exploration), while the domestic Indian power and ferro-alloy businesses face a softening price cycle.
summary.business: Nava manufactures manganese ferro alloys (Silico Manganese and Ferro Silicon) at smelters in Paloncha, Telangana and Dhenkanal, Odisha, and generates thermal power through captive and independent power plants in India and through Maamba Energy Limited in Zambia, which operates the country's only large-scale integrated coal-fired 300 MW power plant alongside its largest coal mine. Alloy output is sold to Japanese steel mills under long-term annual contracts and to major Indian steel producers under quarterly fixed-base contracts, while Zambian power is sold to state utility ZESCO Limited under a 20-year PPA and coal is sold externally to industrial consumers. The Group is also building a commercial agriculture platform in Zambia (avocado plantation and an integrated sugar complex), runs an O&M services business for thermal assets, distributes women's health and wellness products in Southeast Asia, and holds manganese and lithium exploration interests in Cote d'Ivoire and Zambia.

Mining: Coal (Maamba mine, captive and external sales)
Healthcare: Women's health and wellness products distributed through Compai Pharma in Malaysia and Singapore
Agri-Business: Avocados (Division A first commercial harvest, exported to South Africa)
Integrated sugar complex - sugar, distillery and co-generation power (under construction)
Services: Operations and Maintenance (O&M) services for thermal power assets

currentContext.expansion: Nava's expansion pipeline is concentrated in Zambia and spans power, renewables and commercial agriculture. Maamba Energy Limited's Phase II 300 MW brownfield thermal power plant is under construction with a capex outlay of USD 400 million, of which US$ 290 million of debt funding is tied up with Zambian banks and financial institutions; commissioning is targeted for Q4 FY 2027 (the January-March 2027 window), the PPA with ZESCO covers 100% of Phase II net capacity at 9.5 US cents per kilowatt hour, Nava Energy Pte Ltd has been appointed O&M Contractor, and at full year operation the plant is expected to generate USD 180-200 million in annual revenues. The 100 MW solar project under Maamba Solar Energy Limited marks the Group's entry into a renewable energy portfolio, with total capex of US$ 90 million and US$ 63 million of debt tied up, commissioning scheduled to commence in July 2026 (targeted July-August 2026), a signed 20-year PPA with ZESCO at 7.80 US cents per kilowatt hour, Nava Energy Zambia Limited as O&M Contractor, and expected revenue of USD 20-22 million at full operation. Together these represent the 400 MW of power capacity addition on which management says early-commissioning focus remains, and the increase in consolidated debt during the year reflects term-loan drawdowns for both projects. In commercial agriculture, the Nava Avocado plantation achieved its first commercial harvest of over 150 MT from Division A exported to South Africa, with over 250,000 plants planted as at March 2026, the full plantation of 400,000 trees to be completed by May 2027, a state-of-the-art packhouse under construction, Global GAP certification for Division A, expected yield of approximately 1,200+ MT in FY 2026-27 roughly doubling each year thereafter through 2034, and a target fruit yield of about 25,000 MT at peak tree maturity. Kawambwa Sugar Limited's integrated sugar complex - sugarcane plantation over 4,500 Ha, 2,500 TCD sugar processing, a 30 KLPD distillery and a 20 MW co-generation power plant - began construction during the year with land development and plantation activity underway and all major packages ordered, targeted for commissioning by March 2028, with debt financing being worked upon with bilateral financial institutions and banks. Overall project progress on the Phase II thermal expansion and avocado plantation crossed the 50% mark during the year and is nearing completion phase by March 2027. Alongside greenfield build-out, the existing base was reconfigured rather than expanded: 60 MW at Odisha was converted from captive to independent power plant mode with effect from 01 November 2025, taking the 150 MW station to 30 MW CPP / 120 MW IPP, and two Telangana furnaces were shifted from Ferro Silicon to Silico Manganese, with the installed metals set-up offering flexibility to produce up to approximately 160,000 MT. Upstream, the Company holds a 340 square kilometre manganese ore concession in Cote d'Ivoire where metallurgical studies are underway ahead of an exploitation permit, and lithium exploration continues in the Mapatizya area of Zambia subject to regulatory clarity on an overlapping licence claim.

risks.risk: Sector-specific and market risk - ferro alloys exposure to the steel demand cycle, export-market weakness, commodity price volatility, power tariff movements and geopolitical uncertainty
risks.note: The Metals division's realisations track the steel cycle and export access; during the year EU quota measures, US tariffs and Middle East disruption redirected export-grade material into the domestic market and compressed realisations. Mitigated by continuous monitoring, a flexible product mix, long-term contracts and geographic diversification.

risks.risk: Commercial risk - pressure on realisations, freight costs, customer payment delays and spot-market exposure
risks.note: Domestic ferro alloy prices remained subdued with intense competition from marginal players, and payment behaviour of large offtakers directly affects working capital. Mitigated by credit assessment, contractual enforcement, Letter of Credit mechanisms and prudent bidding, with spot exposure held to only 10-15% of output.

risks.risk: Financial risk - cost and availability of capital, foreign exchange volatility, and deferred tax movements arising from currency appreciation
risks.note: The Group funds large Zambian projects with tied-up term debt and reports in INR across USD and Kwacha exposures; the Kwacha's appreciation drove a deferred tax provision that materially reduced reported consolidated profit even though it is a timing difference. Mitigated by disciplined capital allocation, project finance discipline, hedging and calibrated dividend decisions.

risks.risk: Business risk - fuel availability and pricing, manganese ore and reductant availability, and project execution risk
risks.note: Alloy and power economics both hinge on coal and ore input security, and a large share of group value now sits in projects still under construction. Mitigated by the mine-to-mouth coal model at Maamba, backward integration via the Ivory Coast manganese ore mine and phased project execution.

risks.risk: Regulatory risk - power sector regulations, Zambian statutory instruments and the Zambia elections in August 2026
risks.note: A large part of earnings sits in a single foreign jurisdiction where tariff, tax and statutory frameworks can change, as shown by MEL's power division moving to a 15% effective tax rate on completion of its tax holiday. Mitigated by regulatory engagement, legal and compliance oversight and ring-fencing of USD power assets.

risks.risk: Counterparty risk - ZESCO payment terms and potential PPA renegotiation
risks.note: MEL sells power to a single state utility offtaker under a 20-year PPA; arrears had built to US$ 160.6 million before being recovered under an Arbitral Award, with receivables now reduced to US$ 28.0 million. Mitigated by bilateral engagement and the arbitration precedent.

risks.risk: Environment and climate risk - agriculture exposure to weather and energy transition policies
risks.note: The new commercial agriculture platform is weather-dependent while the thermal power base faces transition policy pressure, and lower daytime merchant tariffs from rising solar generation plus a projected below-average monsoon are already flagged watch items. Mitigated by insurance, agronomic controls, irrigation, site-level monitoring and diversification into solar.

risks.risk: Project execution and commissioning concentration - a large pipeline of Zambian projects due within a narrow window
risks.note: The 100 MW solar plant, the 300 MW Phase II thermal plant, the avocado plantation build-out and the Kawambwa integrated sugar complex are all in construction simultaneously, funded partly by drawn term loans; the Enterprise Risk Management framework identifies project execution risk explicitly and responds with phased project execution.

one-line thesis: Cash-rich, founder-run conglomerate where Zambian thermal IPP (Maamba) drives consolidated profit and funds a multi-pronged diversification (300MW thermal expansion, 100MW solar, sugar, avocado, lithium/mineral exploration), while the domestic Indian power and ferro-alloy businesses face a softening price cycle.

guidance (forward):
- **Q4 FY26 Indian power**: "more or less fully committed" on tie-ups for summer.
- **Q1 FY27 Indian power**: in process of tying up most surplus quantities.
- **Ferro-alloys**: pricing +8% from Q3 into current Q4; mgmt expects prices "stable" rather than rising sharply — low-margin but good top line.
- **300MW thermal (Zambia) + 100MW solar**: full-year operations from FY27-28. Full-year revenue at steady state — thermal $180–200m, solar $15–16m.
- **Sugar (KSL) processing unit**: complete ~April 2028 (mid-2028).
- **Avocado**: full production from all 4 divisions over an 8-year horizon; significant revenue contribution 4–5 years out.
order book & pipeline:
- Long-term 5-year bilateral PPA with Tamil Nadu for 60MW IPP plant in Odisha at INR5.2/kWh.
- Targeting similar long-term/short-term allocations for other domestic units to reduce exchange-price volatility.
- Maamba supplying Phase 1 & Phase 2 PPAs in Zambia; govt diversifying away from hydro.
segment / subsidiary:
- **Maamba Energy (MEL)**: core profit engine; 97% PLF; arrears down, $30.5m outstanding receivable remaining; 300MW Phase-2 expansion underway.
- **Nava Global**: completed $50m buyback funded by Maamba dividends; remains 100% Nava-owned (buyback reduced capital, no ownership change).
- **Indian power**: planned shutdowns at several plants this quarter dampened PLF; domestic price/demand softening.
- **Ferro-alloys**: weak profitability; manganese sourced mostly outside India, minimal MOIL exposure (only small fines, no lumps) so MOIL's 5% price hike is immaterial.
growth verticals / optionality:
- 100MW Zambia solar ($90m capex, 10–12 yr payback); potential additional solar phase later.
- Avocado plantation (4 divisions × 275 ha; first pilot crop 140 MT; $55m commitment).
- Kawambwa Sugar Ltd ($100m commitment).
- Ivory Coast 360 sq km mineral concession — under exploration, no discovery disclosed.
- Lithium mines in Africa — exploration stage.
- Nacharam land (65 acres, Hyderabad) — rising market value, unmonetized optionality.
margins & cost dynamics:
- EBITDA margin expansion to 48.3% almost entirely MEL PLF-driven (97%), not cost reversal.
- Domestic exchange power price down ~12% YoY — margin headwind mitigated via long-term contracts.
- Ferro-alloys structurally low-margin; +8% price recovery into Q4 but EBIT near breakeven.

capital allocation:
- $50m Nava Global buyback completed via Maamba dividend upstreaming.
- Stated priority: retain cash for greenfield/expansion funding first, then corporate actions (generous dividends/buybacks "to boost shareholder confidence").
- Net debt ~$200m at 9M FY26 — modest given asset base.
risks & watch-items:
- Domestic merchant power price/demand decline (~12% YoY exchange price drop).
- Ferro-alloys at near-breakeven; cyclical, low-margin.
- Maamba arrears ($30.5m outstanding) and Zambia sovereign/FX exposure (other income swings on FX).
- Long-gestation diversification (avocado 8 yrs, sugar to 2028, lithium/Ivory Coast unproven) ties up capital with distant payback.
- Solar payback 10–12 years — low IRR optionality.
management quality / tone: - Confident, candid; openly acknowledged domestic power weakness and ferro-alloy underperformance rather than spinning. Clear capital-allocation discipline (buyback funded by subsidiary dividend, debt kept modest). Founder family (Devineni) deeply involved across operations and strategy.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Consolidated profitability is highly leveraged to a single asset (Maamba PLF) — 97% PLF this quarter flatters margins; normalization or shutdowns will compress.
- A large chunk of the other-income beat (~INR30 cr) is non-cash FX and not sustainable — headline PAT growth overstates operating momentum.
- The India business is effectively being de-risked into long-term PPAs (TN at INR5.2/kWh) to escape volatile exchange pricing.
- Significant hidden optionality (65-acre Nacharam land, lithium, Ivory Coast minerals) carried at no/low recognized value.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Nava manufactures manganese ferro alloys (Silico Manganese and Ferro Silicon) at smelters in Paloncha, Telangana and Dhenkanal, Odisha, and generates thermal power through captive and independent power plants in India and through Maamba Energy Limited in Zambia, which operates the country's only large-scale integrated coal-fired 300 MW power plant alongside its largest coal mine. Alloy output is sold to Japanese steel mills under long-term annual contracts and to major Indian steel producers under quarterly fixed-base contracts, while Zambian power is sold to state utility ZESCO Limited under a 20-year PPA and coal is sold externally to industrial consumers. The Group is also building a commercial agriculture platform in Zambia (avocado plantation and an integrated sugar complex), runs an O&M services business for thermal assets, distributes women's health and wellness products in Southeast Asia, and holds manganese and lithium exploration interests in Cote d'Ivoire and Zambia.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India expected to remain the fastest-growing large steel-demand market in 2026 and 2027, providing a positive backdrop for domestic ferroalloy demand
- Government capital expenditure growth, continuing infrastructure upgrade, strong automobile momentum with GST rationalisation and India's trade deals with developed economies supporting steel-industry momentum
- Domestic ferro alloy market expected to be quite stable given the uptick in Indian steel demand, though continued weak export markets and trade barriers keep pressure on domestic realisations
- Reduction in captive power tariffs expected to improve the competitiveness and margins of the Metals division
- Decrease in Singareni Collieries coal prices and higher power plant operating parameters at Odisha to show positive effect in FY 2026-27
- Management does not anticipate any reason for ferro alloy prices to fall meaningfully below the preceding year on a full-year basis, though pricing remains fluid
- Indian power demand growth driven by robust economic expansion, urbanisation and increased local manufacturing, with emerging demand from electric vehicles, data centres and AI-driven infrastructure
- Availability of medium-term PPA, lower Singareni coal prices and the conversion of 60 MW into IPP to compound through FY 2026-27
- Watch item: reduced merchant tariffs during daytime on power exchanges due to a substantial increase in solar generation, plus a projected below-average monsoon and dry spells, affecting remunerative tariffs
- Power deficit in Zambia and Southern African nations keeps MEL's 300 MW plant operating at full capacity; commissioning of the 100 MW solar and 300 MW thermal plants may reduce those deficits and boost economic activity
- Group to see additional revenues during the year from the expected commissioning of the 100 MW solar and 300 MW thermal plants, while lower ECL reversal and Kwacha appreciation will weigh on MEL's power division profitability
- Demand for high grade coal expected to increase with improved economic activity as power deficits reduce; competition from nearby mines addressed through increased marketing efforts and pricing strategy
- Avocado yields scaling with tree growth, with Division B expected to give a trial yield in the current year
- Ferro alloys industry closely linked to the steel demand cycle, with divergence across regions - China declining while developing economies, ASEAN, MENA and Africa show renewed momentum
- Approximately 40% of Metals production sold under long-term annual contracts with Japanese mills and 40-50% under quarterly fixed-base contracts with major Indian steel producers, limiting spot-market exposure to only 10-15% of output
- Maamba Energy Limited holds a 20-year Power Purchase Agreement with ZESCO Limited, supplying power since 2016
- PPA with ZESCO for 100% of Phase II net capacity is in place at 9.5 US cents per kilowatt hour
- 20-year PPA with ZESCO for the 100 MW solar project signed at 7.80 US cents per kilowatt hour
- Five-year Power Purchase Agreement for 50 MW of Odisha capacity starting February 2026, plus bilateral contracts supporting Indian merchant power volumes
- Nava Energy Pte Ltd appointed O&M Contractor for MEL's Phase II 300 MW expansion and Nava Energy Zambia Limited appointed O&M Contractor for MSEL's 100 MW solar project

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Nava's expansion pipeline is concentrated in Zambia and spans power, renewables and commercial agriculture. Maamba Energy Limited's Phase II 300 MW brownfield thermal power plant is under construction with a capex outlay of USD 400 million, of which US$ 290 million of debt funding is tied up with Zambian banks and financial institutions; commissioning is targeted for Q4 FY 2027 (the January-March 2027 window), the PPA with ZESCO covers 100% of Phase II net capacity at 9.5 US cents per kilowatt hour, Nava Energy Pte Ltd has been appointed O&M Contractor, and at full year operation the plant is expected to generate USD 180-200 million in annual revenues. The 100 MW solar project under Maamba Solar Energy Limited marks the Group's entry into a renewable energy portfolio, with total capex of US$ 90 million and US$ 63 million of debt tied up, commissioning scheduled to commence in July 2026 (targeted July-August 2026), a signed 20-year PPA with ZESCO at 7.80 US cents per kilowatt hour, Nava Energy Zambia Limited as O&M Contractor, and expected revenue of USD 20-22 million at full operation. Together these represent the 400 MW of power capacity addition on which management says early-commissioning focus remains, and the increase in consolidated debt during the year reflects term-loan drawdowns for both projects. In commercial agriculture, the Nava Avocado plantation achieved its first commercial harvest of over 150 MT from Division A exported to South Africa, with over 250,000 plants planted as at March 2026, the full plantation of 400,000 trees to be completed by May 2027, a state-of-the-art packhouse under construction, Global GAP certification for Division A, expected yield of approximately 1,200+ MT in FY 2026-27 roughly doubling each year thereafter through 2034, and a target fruit yield of about 25,000 MT at peak tree maturity. Kawambwa Sugar Limited's integrated sugar complex - sugarcane plantation over 4,500 Ha, 2,500 TCD sugar processing, a 30 KLPD distillery and a 20 MW co-generation power plant - began construction during the year with land development and plantation activity underway and all major packages ordered, targeted for commissioning by March 2028, with debt financing being worked upon with bilateral financial institutions and banks. Overall project progress on the Phase II thermal expansion and avocado plantation crossed the 50% mark during the year and is nearing completion phase by March 2027. Alongside greenfield build-out, the existing base was reconfigured rather than expanded: 60 MW at Odisha was converted from captive to independent power plant mode with effect from 01 November 2025, taking the 150 MW station to 30 MW CPP / 120 MW IPP, and two Telangana furnaces were shifted from Ferro Silicon to Silico Manganese, with the installed metals set-up offering flexibility to produce up to approximately 160,000 MT. Upstream, the Company holds a 340 square kilometre manganese ore concession in Cote d'Ivoire where metallurgical studies are underway ahead of an exploitation permit, and lithium exploration continues in the Mapatizya area of Zambia subject to regulatory clarity on an overlapping licence claim.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Mine-to-mouth integrated coal and power model at Maamba provides fuel security, cost stability and independence from global coal market dynamics, while contributing external revenue beyond the captive requirement
- Contracting discipline in Metals: approximately 40% of production sold under long-term annual contracts with Japanese mills and 40-50% under quarterly fixed-base contracts with major Indian steel producers, limiting spot-market exposure to only 10-15% of output

- Captive power integration in India, with 144 MW earmarked for captive consumption in ferro alloy production, and downward-revised captive tariffs improving alloy cost competitiveness
- Proven O&M capability in thermal power, evidenced by MEL's sustained high plant availability and PLF, leading to O&M mandates for the Phase II 300 MW expansion and the 100 MW solar project
- Product-mix flexibility across Silico Manganese and Ferro Silicon, allowing the Metals division to shift furnaces towards whichever alloy market conditions favour
- Deliberate long-cycle capital allocation - deploying capital where barriers to entry are high and staying through the gestation period, producing diversification across geographies, cycles and sectors
